newsitem.title: LEBANON: Mixed trade on Beirut Stock Exchange.
newsitem.headline: Mixed trade on Beirut Stock Exchange.

text.p: Trade was mixed in higher turnover on the Beirut Stock Exchange on Wednesday with five shares unchanged, one falling, one rising and no trade in another.
The only shares to move were Solidere B which rose to $10.875 in heavy demand and Bank of Beirut which fell back to $3.9375 from Tuesday's record high of $4.
The two other bank shares, Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce and Banque Audi, were unchanged at their alltime highs of $18.25 and $23.125 respectively.
The LIBX bank index fell 0.52 percent to 154.21. The LISPI general index fell 0.04 percent to 89.78 while the BLOM general index rose 0.31 percent to 946.46.
Market turnover rose to 229,392 shares for a value of $1,819,211 from 213,212 shares and $1,355,106 on Tuesday.
Solidere B rose on demand of 133,787 against supply of 26,732 on the first fixing and demand of 128,017 against supply of 31,846 on the second fixing. Turnover totalled 24,904.
"There was no supply at $10.75 on the second fixing which indicates the share might go up slightly," a broker who asked not to be identified said.
"The period of Solidere consolidation will last longer because those buying are not willing to bid up," he said.
Solidere A were unchanged at $10.75. They fell to $10.5 on the first fixing but recovered at the second fixing.
Some 20,000 BOB shares changed hands in block trading at $4 on the floor while 5,000 BLC shares traded at between $18 amd $18.125. Outside the floor, a block of 24,060 Audi shares traded at $23.125.
Of the four industrial firms, Ciments Libanais and pipemaker Eternit were unchanged at $1.28125 and $2 respectively.
There was no trade in tilemaker Uniceramic and Ciments Blancs.
